messages:
maria: FYI saw a weird cascade this morning — cluster-a in us-west1 hit GPU quota, CA started provisioning in cluster-b (us-central) and cluster-c (europe-west). Ended up with cross-region fallbacks and higher egress costs. Need a short plan: quota preflight + warm standby pool?

devon: Ugh. Seen that pattern before. Can we add a cheap 'standby' pool of small GPU nodes (e.g. a single 8G GPU with very low priority) in each region to absorb bursts? Scale policy: keep 0->1 warm node within 2m.

sophie: Agree on standby. Also we should preflight quota before CA triggers big creates. Something like: run a quick quota check job that queries GCP APIs and short-circuits cross-cluster scaleouts if regional quota is available within X.

maria: +1. Proposal: before creating nodes in other regions, check quotas and network egress budget. If quota is exhausted in origin region, spin standby in same region for a short window, else allow cross-region with a flag. 

infra-bot: ALERT: gpu-quota-limit-hit cluster-a us-west1 2026-02-21T09:12:07Z (auto-detected) :warning:

devon: Rough sketch of the quota preflight command: 
```bash
# simple quota check
gcloud compute regions describe us-west1 --format="json(quotas)" | jq '.quotas[] | select(.metric=="GPUS")'
```
If remaining>=requested then allow local scaling. Else fallback to standby warmpool then cross-region.

sophie: For autoscaler config, bump the scaleDownDelay and only allow scale-down after warmpool drain to avoid oscillation. Example nodepool config: 
```yaml
nodePool:
  name: gpu-standby
  autoscaling:
    enabled: true
    minNodeCount: 0
    maxNodeCount: 2
    scaleDownDelay: 10m
    scaleUpPolicy: "fast"
```

jordan: Also watch networking — when we did cross-region fallback earlier, some customers hit HA proxy timeouts due to increased RTT and egress limits. We should prefer same-region warmpool even if small hit to cost. Maybe implement a cost threshold: only allow cross-region if expected egress+latency cost < 2x local standby cost.

maria: Good call. I'll draft a runbook: quota preflight -> try local warmpool (0->1 within 90s) -> if local capacity still insufficient and cost threshold OK, allow cross-region failover. Include metrics to monitor: quota_hits, warmpool_activations, cross_region_fallbacks, added_egress_cost.

devon: Can we add a pre-provision check into the CA webhook? Pseudocode: 
```python
def allow_node_creation(region, gpu_count):
  if not check_quota(region, gpu_count):
    return try_warmpool(region)
  return True
```

sophie: Also add a short TTL label on warmpool nodes so they get reclaimed quickly if unused. :recycle:

maria: I'll open a short RFC and a runbook in GH. Tagging @oncall for visibility. Thanks everyone.
